Two distinctions now guide the work: the residual tube can move with a cancellation if its full framing and upper gluing are transported, and the charged disk has to be tested in its own metric. I’m checking whether compact control of its collar turns small Cotton and umbilicity defects into a finite energy comparison.

The two handle orders now have a common recognition test. If either actual intermediate boundary admits positive scalar curvature, the winding-one order gives \(S^3\) and the winding-zero order gives \(\#_2(S^1\times S^2)\). The latter case needed a separate filling argument. On the variational side, the cutoff calculation rules out an exactly round, umbilic boundary on every sufficiently late charged disk of a hypothetical nonstandard type.

**Positive scalar curvature on either intermediate cut recognizes the standard smooth sphere** in a normalized mixed presentation with one 1-handle, two 2-handles and one 3-handle. If the winding-one attachment goes first, its cut must be \(S^3\). If the winding-zero attachment goes first, its cut must be \(\#_2(S^1\times S^2)\). The second order required a separate filling argument to rule out additional homology-sphere summands. A sufficient test on an actual marked product band is \((\min R)d^2\ge 3\pi^2\), where \(d\) is the distance between its ends inside the band. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn167318677view3","turn167318677view2","turn468372483view1"]}}

The marked control and its framed slide were checked in both orders, carrying the residual tube and upper gluing. With **three middle handles** and one lower 1-handle, a successful winding-one cut reduces the count from three to two on the same smooth type. If the next intermediate cut also admits positive scalar curvature, the returned two-component link recognizes the original sphere.

**The charged disk gives an obstruction.** At a fixed positive subcritical source, an exactly conformally round, umbilic disk boundary forces
\[
E_+(g_i;D_i)=E_-(g_i;D_i)\le e_i-I^+(M).
\]
The proof shrinks the two widths at that fixed index, keeps the joined peak strictly below \(8\pi^2\), and caps the complete exterior on the original smooth type. Since the selected disk retains a fixed positive mass while the minimizing excess tends to zero, every sufficiently late selected disk fails the exact-face condition.

The first uncovered mixed class has no verified reducing move or positive-scalar-curvature witness on either marked cut. On the variational route, a finite repair that pays the full exterior cost remains open, as does subcritical entry on arbitrary smooth types.

The parent paper makes one consequence explicit. On a positive subcritical source, an exactly conformally round, umbilic separating sphere forces the two raw chiral masses to agree **on each side separately**. For the master’s parametrized charged disk, the capped exterior has the original smooth type, so the disk mass is at most the minimizing excess \(e_i-I^+(M)\). That excess tends to zero while the selected disk retains a fixed positive mass. An exact face is therefore excluded at every sufficiently late selected index.

Each paper ends with its outstanding challenges. On the handle side, the first missing step is selecting a reducing move or a recognizing intermediate boundary on an untreated presentation. On the metric side, it is constructing a repair on the actual charged source that pays the complete exterior cost while keeping the joined path strictly subcritical. Applying that argument to arbitrary smooth types also requires positive subcritical entry.

All three PDFs compiled without warnings or unresolved references, and the repository link check passed. The public chat archive could not be refreshed because the exact conversation source was unavailable.
